class dsbXML(BaseModel):
    """Root element of DesignBuilder XML file.

    Represents the top-level dsbXML element containing metadata and simulation data
    for a DesignBuilder project.

    Attributes:
        name: Name of the DesignBuilder project
        date: Creation/modification date of the file
        version: Version of the DesignBuilder format
        objects: Number of objects in the model
        site: The site definition containing buildings and geometry
    """
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    name: str = attr()
    date: datetime.date = attr()
    version: str = attr()
    objects: str = attr()
    site: Optional["Site"] = element(default=None)

    @classmethod
    def from_xml(cls, source: str | bytes) -> "dsbXML":
        """Override to handle PascalCase XML tags to snake_case Python fields"""
        from lxml import etree
        if isinstance(source, (str, bytes)):
            root = etree.fromstring(source)
        else:
            root = source

        # Rename PascalCase child elements to lowercase (iterative, non-recursive)
        # This handles XML like <Site> being mapped to field 'site'
        stack = [root]
        while stack:
            element = stack.pop()
            # Convert tag names: Site -> site, Tables -> tables, etc.
            if element.tag and len(element.tag) > 1 and element.tag[0].isupper():
                element.tag = element.tag[0].lower() + element.tag[1:]
            # Add children to stack for processing
            stack.extend(reversed(element))

        instance = super().from_xml_tree(root)
        return instance

    def to_xml(self, **kwargs) -> str | bytes:
        """Override to output dsbXML as root element"""
        from lxml import etree
        xml_output = super().to_xml(**kwargs)
        if isinstance(xml_output, bytes):
            root = etree.fromstring(xml_output)
            root.tag = "dsbXML"
            return bytes(etree.tostring(root, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8"))
        else:
            root = etree.fromstring(xml_output.encode())
            root.tag = "dsbXML"
            return str(etree.tostring(root, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8").decode("UTF-8"))

class Point3D(BaseModel):
    """A 3D point in space.

    Represents coordinates with cached property accessors for x, y, z values.
    Internally stores coordinates as a semicolon-separated string.

    Attributes:
        value: Semicolon-separated coordinates as string (e.g., "10.5;20.3;5.0")
    """
    value: str

    _coords_cache: Union[tuple[float, float, float], None] = None

    @property
    def _cached_coords(self) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
        if self._coords_cache is None:
            parsed = tuple(float(c) for c in self.value.split(";"))
            assert len(parsed) == 3, "Expected 3 coordinates"
            object.__setattr__(self, "_coords_cache", tuple(parsed))
        assert self._coords_cache is not None
        return self._coords_cache

    @property
    def x(self) -> float:
        return float(self._cached_coords[0])

    @property
    def y(self) -> float:
        return float(self._cached_coords[1])

    @property
    def z(self) -> float:
        return float(self._cached_coords[2])

    @property
    def coords(self) -> List[float]:
        return list(self._cached_coords)

    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Union[float, List[float]]) -> None:
        if name == "coords":
            if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 3:
                self.value = ";".join(map(str, value))
            else:
                raise ValueError("Coordinates must be a list of 3 numbers")
        elif name in ["x", "y", "z"]:
            index = {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 2}[name]
            coords = self.value.split(";")
            coords[index] = str(value)
            self.value = ";".join(coords)
        else:
            # Invalidate cache when value string changes
            if name == "value":
                object.__setattr__(self, "_coords_cache", None)
            super().__setattr__(name, value)

class Table(BaseModel):
    """A single data table with named fields and rows.

    Represents simulation data such as climate, schedules, or other tabular information.
    Provides access to rows by index and columns by field name.

    Attributes:
        name: Table name/identifier
        numberOfFields: Number of columns in the table
        category: Optional category classification for the table
        field_name: Names of each column/field
        rows: List of data rows
    """

    name: str = attr()
    numberOfFields: int = attr()
    category: Optional[List[str]] = element(tag="Category", default=None)
    field_name: List[str] = element(tag="FieldName")
    rows: Optional[List[TableRow]] = element(tag="Row", default=None)

    @field_validator("category", mode="before")
    def parse_category(cls, value: Optional[str | List]) -> Optional[List[str]]:
        if value is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(value, str):
            return [value]
        return value

    def __getitem__(self, index: int) -> "TableRow":
        """Get a specific row by index"""
        if self.rows is None or index >= len(self.rows):
            raise IndexError("Table row index out of range")
        return self.rows[index]

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> List[str]:
        """Get all values for a specific field by name"""
        try:
            field_index = self.field_name.index(name)
        except ValueError:
            raise AttributeError(
                f"'{self.__class__.__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
            )

        if self.rows is None:
            return []

        return [row.cells[field_index] for row in self.rows]

    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """Set values for a specific field by name"""
        # Let Pydantic handle special attributes
        if name in self.__dict__ or name.startswith("_"):
            super().__setattr__(name, value)
            return

        # Handle field_name and rows specially
        if name in ("field_name", "rows", "name", "numberOfFields", "category"):
            super().__setattr__(name, value)
            return

        # Handle custom field setting
        if self.rows is not None and name in self.field_name:
            field_index = self.field_name.index(name)
            if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == len(self.rows):
                for i, row in enumerate(self.rows):
                    row.cells[field_index] = value[i]
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Value must be a list with {len(self.rows)} elements")
        else:
            raise AttributeError(
                f"'{self.__class__.__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'"
            )

class ObjectIDs(BaseModel):
    """Unique identifiers for DesignBuilder model objects.

    Maintains a hierarchical system of handles to track object relationships
    throughout the model. Rules:
    1. All defined handles must be unique integers
    2. Undefined handle is -1
    3. Site handle is always the max current handle
    4. Each ObjectID is given new handle on creation

    Attributes:
        handle: Globally unique object handle (auto-generated)
        buildingHandle: Reference to parent building (-1 if undefined)
        buildingBlockHandle: Reference to parent building block (-1 if undefined)
        zoneHandle: Reference to parent zone (-1 if undefined)
        surfaceIndex: Index of surface within parent zone (-1 if undefined)
        openingIndex: Index of opening within parent surface (-1 if undefined)
    """

    handle: int = Field(default_factory=generate_site_handle)
    buildingHandle: int = attr(default=-1)
    buildingBlockHandle: int = attr(default=-1)
    zoneHandle: int = attr(default=-1)
    surfaceIndex: int = attr(default=-1)
    openingIndex: int = attr(default=-1)

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        populate_by_name=True,
    )

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text:
Complete API reference for all DesignBuilder Schema Pydantic models.

The DesignBuilder Schema library provides a comprehensive set of type-safe models for working with DesignBuilder files. All models are built on Pydantic v2 and support both XML and JSON serialization.

docs.title: Model Organization
docs.text:
Models are organized into logical modules:

  • core.py - Core building models: Site, Building, Zone, Surface
  • geometry.py - 3D geometry: Point3D, Line, Vertices
  • attributes.py - Named and key-value attributes
  • tables.py - Simulation tables and schedules
  • hvac/ - Complete HVAC system models:
  • network.py - HVAC loops and connections
  • components.py - Equipment: boilers, chillers, pumps
  • unit_components.py - Unitary systems
  • zone_components.py - Zone-level equipment
  • id.py - Object identification system

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Type-Safe: Full type hints for IDE autocompletion
  • Validated: Pydantic validation on all inputs
  • Documented: Comprehensive docstrings with examples
  • Optimized: Slots-enabled for memory efficiency
  • Serializable: XML and JSON support via pydantic-xml

See the Models page for complete class documentation.
